sections.html:
Trumbull is a Fairfield County town in the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region, bordering Bridgeport, Shelton, Stratford, Fairfield, Easton and Monroe. It had 36,827 residents at the 2020 census and covers 23.5 square miles.

The land runs from about 40 feet above sea level at Beach Park to 615 feet at the top of Monitor Hill, so a house may stand on level ground near the Pequonnock River or on a hillside lot. The two sell differently, and buyers will ask about grading and drainage on the second kind.

The big population jump came after the war: 8,641 people in 1950, 20,379 in 1960 and 31,394 in 1970. A good share of the houses likely date from those decades. Your deed and the assessor's record show the year yours was built.

Trumbull is a town of villages and has no single downtown. They are Trumbull Center, Long Hill, Nichols, Daniels Farm and Tashua. The Nichols Farms Historic District and the Christ Episcopal Church and Tashua Burial Ground are on the National Register, so if your house is within the Nichols Farms district, ask the town what that means for exterior changes before you plan work.

Green space is a real selling point. The town has 871.23 acres of park facilities, including Twin Brooks Park, Indian Ledge Park and Robert G. Beach Memorial Park, along with the 382-acre Pequonnock River Valley State Park and the 268-acre Tashua Recreation Facility with its golf course. If your house sits near a park or trail, say so.

RouteWhat it does in Trumbull
Route 8Freeway through the southeast part of town toward Waterbury and Interstate 84
Route 15 (Merritt Parkway)Runs east to New Haven and west toward New York City
Route 25North to south, joins Route 8 at the Bridgeport line
Route 108Nichols Avenue and Huntington Turnpike, north from Stratford
Route 111Main Street, from Bridgeport's North End to Monroe
Route 127White Plains Road and Church Hill Road through the town center

No Metro-North station is in town. The closest are Bridgeport at 4.6 miles, Stratford at 4.9 and Fairfield-Black Rock at 5.7, all on the New Haven Line. Greater Bridgeport Transit Authority runs the buses. Buyers who commute care about that distance, so state it.

Trumbull Public Schools has Trumbull High School, two middle schools (Hillcrest and Madison) and six elementary schools: Booth Hill, Daniels Farm, Frenchtown, Jane Ryan, Middlebrook and Tashua. Families will want to know which one serves the address.

Fire protection comes from three all-volunteer departments: the Long Hill Fire District, the Nichols Fire District and the Trumbull Center Fire District. Each handles its own tax structure and fundraising, so your tax bill may include a district line. Check the current bill or ask the tax collector, and tell the buyer.

Westfield Trumbull mall sits on Route 111 at the Bridgeport line, and an office park north of the Merritt Parkway near the Shelton and Stratford borders has housed firms such as UnitedHealthcare. Planning rules include professional office overlay zones along White Plains Road, Church Hill Road and Main Street, and a mixed-use zone around the historic Long Hill Green. If you own property along those corridors, confirm current zoning with the town.

When the deed is recorded in Trumbull, the seller's side files Connecticut Form OP-236 with the town clerk. The grantor, the grantor's attorney or an agent can file it, and the return and any tax are due at recording. Trumbull's code on the form is 144.

Tax applies when the consideration reaches $2,000, unless an exemption applies. Towns on myCTREC take the return electronically, and others take paper copies with a check payable to the Commissioner of Revenue Services.

  • A principal residence deeded in lieu of foreclosure is exempt.
  • A principal residence sold for too little to pay the mortgages and priority liens is exempt.
  • A principal residence with a deteriorated concrete foundation caused by pyrrhotite, as determined by a professional engineer, is exempt, and a copy of the engineer's evaluation goes with the return.
  • Schedule A is added if there are more than two grantors or an estate or trust is selling.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so the offer is based on the house as it is and closing depends on title work and the date you choose. You send us the address and the condition, and we respond with an offer you can accept or turn down.

It suits a house with deferred work, an estate property or a tenant situation. For a buyer who needs financing, the same flaws can slow things at inspection or appraisal. If the house is in good shape and you have time, a listing with an agent may bring a different result, and we say so plainly.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you sell
sections.html:
1. Find the deed and the build year, and pull the mortgage statement and latest tax bill.
  2. Ask the tax collector whether any fire district charge or other balance is due.
  3. If the seller is an estate or trust, confirm who can sign.
  4. Walk the house and list its known problems honestly, from the roof to the basement.
  5. Hire a closing attorney to run the title search and prepare the OP-236.
  6. Choose a closing date you can meet, and keep the utilities on until then.

On the day of closing, bring photo ID and all keys. Payoffs come out of your proceeds before you receive the remainder. When it is over, keep a copy of the recorded deed and the return.

sections.h2: Selling when the house needs work
sections.html: A worn kitchen, an old roof or a damp basement does not stop a sale, but it changes who buys and how. A buyer with a mortgage faces an appraisal and an inspection, and either can lead to a request for repairs or a lower price. A cash buyer looks at the same house and prices the work in. Neither is wrong. The right choice depends on how much money, time and patience you have.

faqs.a: Fairfield County, in the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region.
About 23.5 square miles, with 36,827 residents at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Is there a train station in Trumbull?
faqs.a: Not in town. The nearest Metro-North stations are Bridgeport (4.6 miles), Stratford (4.9) and Fairfield-Black Rock (5.7).

faqs.q: What do I file with the town clerk when I sell?
faqs.a: Connecticut Form OP-236, the conveyance tax return, when the deed is recorded. Trumbull's town code is 144, and your closing attorney can work out the amount.

faqs.q: Will I need to repair my Trumbull house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash offer is based on the property in its current condition.
